title: Collect Ideas Like Stones

body.heading: Ideas arrive at odd times
paragraphs: Ideas rarely turn up during scheduled “thinking time.” They arrive in showers, on buses, mid-conversation — and they leave quickly, usually within minutes, if nothing catches them.

The difference between people who “have ideas” and people who don't is often just a capture habit: a notebook, a notes app, a voice memo — one trusted place where every fragment goes, however small or silly.

body.heading: Collect now, judge later
paragraphs: Write the idea down in a few words, exactly as it arrived, without evaluating it. Judgement during collection kills the supply; there will be plenty of time to sort the stones later.

Review your collection every week or two. Most entries will stay stones — but combinations appear, and one dull fragment plus another dull fragment sometimes makes the thing you were looking for all along.

takeaway: One notebook, every fragment, no judging — that is an idea system.
